newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares close off in late echo of Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares close off in late echo of Wall Street.

text.p: Chilean shares closed lower on Monday, playing catch up to Wall Street for the session the local market missed on Friday, traders said.
Santiago's 40-share IPSA index closed 0.74 percent down at 131.25 points on low turnover of 7.6 billion pesos, or about $18.2 million.
"The market basically made up for Friday's drop in the New York-listed ADRs," said Jaime Pena y Lillo, portfolio manager at brokers Socimer.
Pena y Lillo added that he saw the Chilean stock market stuck in a rut between 130 and 136 points on the IPSA, already at a premium over other Latin American markets.
Among the worst-hit shares was pharmaceutical company Laboratorios Chile, which dropped 3.33 percent on Monday despite announcing plans to expand operations in Latin America.
Traders said LabChile was still reeling after its general manager quit last week, besides the recent pressure on pharmaceutical stocks.
Among the winners were some of the so-called Chispas investment firms that control a major stake in electricity holding company Enersis.
Chispa company Luz series A shares rose 3.7 percent and Chispauno series A shares gained 1.1 percent.
Spanish utility Empresa Nacional de Electricidad SA on Monday opened a tender to buy all the shares in the Chispas, in a $1.5 billion bid heralded as the deal of the century by the local media.
